step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Inventory: the whiteboard has 14 entities. I kept all of them as separate nodes. No two entities fused into one logical unit: the two S3 buckets have different jobs (one hosts the static web portal, the other is the secure data lake), so they stay separate. 2) Vocabulary mapping: Sanofi SSO -> ThirdParty. The generic 'User' actors are the data scientists using the portal. The pruning rule removes generic human actors, but the User node is an endpoint of a drawn arrow (User <-> CloudFront), and ledger edges and their endpoints cannot be removed. So I kept it and mapped it to UserCompanyAnalyst (internal Sanofi data scientists). R Studio is shown as EC2, as drawn. CloudFormation is mentioned only as the way Service Catalog builds its products, not as an active runtime participant, so I did not add it as a node. Lake Formation is only a possible future service, so I did not add it either. 3) Ledger: there are 12 visual_connections entries. I emitted one edge for each, with the same source and target. 4) Audio-grounded additions: the transcript says users pull data from the Data Lake and process it in RStudio and SageMaker. This gives 2 extra data edges (Data Lake -> R Studio and Data Lake -> SageMaker), so the Data Lake node is not left unconnected. I did not add direct Data Lake -> Translate or Data Lake -> Comprehend edges, because those services are reached through Lambda and a direct edge would skip that step. 5) Flows: Flow 0 is portal access and authentication (User -> CloudFront -> S3 portal, plus Sanofi SSO -> Cognito -> S3 portal). Flow 1 is dynamic API and traceability (S3 portal -> API Gateway -> DynamoDB). Flow 2 is workspace provisioning (S3 portal -> Service Catalog -> R Studio / SageMaker in parallel). Flow 3 is NLP and translation (API Gateway -> Lambda -> Translate / Comprehend Medical in parallel). Flow 4 is data lake consumption (Data Lake -> R Studio / SageMaker in parallel). 6) Self-check: there are 12 visual_connections entries, and I emitted 14 edges (12 from the ledger and 2 grounded in the audio). 14 >= 12.

graph.name: Sanofi Darwin Real World Evidence Data Science Portal on AWS
graph.categories: Healthcare, Data Science, Machine Learning, NLP, Static Web Portal, Self-service Provisioning
graph.notes: Secure data science portal for Sanofi CMO Real World Evidence data scientists, built with partner Teamwork. A static website on S3 is served through CloudFront, which also holds the certificate and lowers costs. Users sign in through Cognito federated with Sanofi SSO. The dynamic part (API Gateway + DynamoDB) records user metadata and every action, so data use is strongly traceable. Service Catalog products built with CloudFormation give each user their own isolated workspace: an encrypted SageMaker notebook with a 100 GB disk, or RStudio. Lambda functions call Translate and Comprehend Medical through the SDK. The Data Lake holds very sensitive data that must stay inside the environment and cannot be downloaded. Each user has a home S3 bucket with predefined access rights. The portal went live in early August; it targeted 5-10 beta testers and grew to 30-40 users in 2-3 weeks.

nodes.name: Sanofi SSO
nodes.notes: Sanofi corporate identity provider, federated with Cognito to authenticate portal users.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: Sanofi Real World Evidence data scientists. About 30-40% of their analyses run on smart/big data sets with RStudio, SageMaker and NLP/translation tools. Usage grew from 5-10 beta testers to 30-40 users within 2-3 weeks.

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Distribution in front of the S3 static website. Lowers costs and holds the TLS certificate.

nodes.name: Cognito
nodes.notes: Identifies users through identity federation with Sanofi SSO.

nodes.name: S3 (Web Portal)
nodes.notes: Static part of the data analytics portal, hosted with the S3 static website feature.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Dynamic part of the portal. Handles the data traceability APIs and NLP/translation requests.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores user metadata and every action performed on the portal, giving strong traceability and audit of each piece of data used in the environment.

nodes.name: Service Catalog
nodes.notes: Portfolio of products (SageMaker, RStudio) that users provision themselves from the portal. Products are built with CloudFormation for repeatable, secure and isolated per-user environments.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Lambda functions that use the AWS SDK to call Translate (mass translation of raw files) and Comprehend Medical (identifying data and metadata in raw files).

nodes.name: R Studio
nodes.notes: RStudio workspace that each user provisions for themselves through Service Catalog.

nodes.name: SageMaker
nodes.notes: One SageMaker notebook per user, encrypted, with a 100 GB disk for data, and traced. Each user can access only their own authorized data set.

nodes.name: Translate
nodes.notes: Mass translation of raw files from a source language detected automatically with Comprehend into a target language chosen by the user.

nodes.name: Comprehend Medical
nodes.notes: Pre-trained service that identifies medical data and metadata in raw files.

nodes.name: Data Lake
nodes.notes: Very sensitive data. It must stay inside the environment and cannot be downloaded to workstations. Data is segregated, encrypted, controlled and audited. Users extract data into their own home S3 bucket, with predefined per-user access rights, and process it in RStudio, SageMaker, Translate or Comprehend.
